$schema.description: Centralized resource catalogue for the Neurodivergence Library. To publish a new resource: (1) drop the file into /public/downloads, then (2) append one object to the `resources` array below. No component changes are required.

fields.title: string — the resource title
fields.description: string — one or two sentence plain-language summary shown on the card
fields.category: string — MUST match one of the values in `categories` exactly
fields.type: string — one of: Whitepaper | Clinical Study | Worksheet | Toolkit
fields.authorOrInstitution: string — author, research group, or publishing institution
fields.downloadUrl: string — path to the file, e.g. /downloads/my-file.pdf (relative to /public)
fields.abstract: string (optional) — longer editorial abstract; shown in the 'Read Abstract' panel and on research cards
fields.featured: boolean (optional) — when true, the resource is surfaced in the 'Cutting-Edge Research' section
fields.readingMinutes: number (optional) — estimated reading time, shown on research cards

resources.title: Executive Function Scaffolding: A Practitioner's Toolkit
resources.description: Structured strategies for externalising working memory, initiation and time-perception — designed for ADHD brains rather than adapted for them.
resources.abstract: This toolkit reframes executive dysfunction not as a deficit of effort but as a difference in the neural regulation of goal-directed behaviour. Drawing on Barkley's model of self-regulation and more recent interest-based nervous-system research, it offers concrete scaffolds — body-doubling, temporal anchoring, and 'externalised intention' cues — that reduce the working-memory load of everyday tasks.

resources.title: Time-Blindness & Task Estimation Worksheet
resources.description: A printable, low-friction worksheet for building a personal reference library of how long tasks actually take versus how long they feel.

resources.title: AuDHD: Living at the Intersection of Two Neurotypes
resources.description: A whitepaper on the lived experience and support needs of people who are both Autistic and ADHD, where regulation strategies can directly conflict.
resources.abstract: The co-occurrence of Autism and ADHD (AuDHD) is now understood to be common rather than exceptional. This paper examines the internal tension of the profile — a nervous system that simultaneously seeks novelty and predictability — and argues for individualised, contradiction-tolerant support plans over one-size-fits-all protocols.

resources.title: Monotropism and the Double Empathy Problem: A Bridging Framework
resources.description: An emerging clinical synthesis linking monotropic attention styles to the mutual, bidirectional nature of cross-neurotype miscommunication.
resources.abstract: The Double Empathy Problem reframes Autistic communication difficulty as a two-way breakdown between neurotypes rather than a one-sided deficit. This study pairs that lens with monotropism theory — the tendency toward deep, singular attention tunnels — to explain why shared context, not social 'skill', is the strongest predictor of successful cross-neurotype interaction.

resources.title: Interoception as the Missing Layer in Sensory Regulation
resources.description: A transdiagnostic clinical study positioning interoceptive awareness — the sense of the body's internal state — as foundational to emotional and sensory regulation.
resources.abstract: Traditional sensory-processing models focus on the external eight senses while under-weighting interoception. This study presents evidence that interoceptive precision predicts self-regulation capacity across ADHD, Autistic and anxious presentations alike, making it a promising transdiagnostic target for neuro-affirming intervention.

resources.title: Sensory Diet Planning Worksheet
resources.description: A calm, grid-based worksheet for mapping sensory inputs across a day and identifying where regulation support is most needed.

resources.title: Recognising the Twice-Exceptional (2e) Learner
resources.description: Why high giftedness and a co-occurring disability so often mask one another — and a framework for identification that looks past averaged test scores.
resources.abstract: Twice-exceptional learners are gifted and also have one or more disabilities. Because strengths and challenges frequently cancel out on standardised measures, these learners are routinely under-identified. This whitepaper offers a strengths-first identification framework and argues for asynchronous, profile-based support.

resources.title: From Remediation to Affirmation: A Paradigm Shift in Practice
resources.description: A landmark study charting the field's move away from deficit-based remediation toward neuro-affirming, identity-first models of support.
resources.abstract: This study documents outcome data from clinics that transitioned from deficit-remediation models to neuro-affirming, strengths-based practice. Across ADHD, Autistic and 2e cohorts, affirmation-first care correlated with lower reported burnout and higher self-advocacy — reframing 'treatment' as accommodation and identity support rather than normalisation.
